body.head: BEBB Editorial Guidelines and Encoding Guide

div.head: Preface
div.p: The Basel Edition of the Bernoulli Correspondence (BEBB) has developed over several phases and will continue to grow until the project ends in 2032. It brings together texts from different phases of the edition. Earlier texts were produced in other formats and later converted to TEI XML. The technology available at the time shaped the way they were edited, and only a normalised version was prepared. Today, a text-faithful version and a normalised version are prepared in parallel.

A text-faithful version is available when the encoding captures essential features of the source, such as the original lineation. A few normalisations added later are insufficient to establish a text-faithful version of the entire text. The editorial and review status is indicated separately.

For texts carried over without further editing, the normalised version remains the only version prepared by the editors. Automatically generated diplomatic views may also be available, and their level of checking against the manuscript is indicated separately. Notices accompanying the texts and in the metadata identify their provenance and editorial status. The notices identifying letters taken from the Bernoulli Wiki are still being completed.

These guidelines build on the 2011 guidelines. They retain the principle of preserving historical spelling as faithfully as possible while making targeted interventions to aid reading. The rules have been developed further for work in TEI XML.

div.head: Purpose and organisation of the guidelines
div.p: The guidelines govern transcription, the establishment of the text, annotation and indexing. The accompanying encoding guide specifies how to implement these practices in TEI XML and record descriptive information in the TEI header.

The guidelines and the BEBB schema together ensure that editorial interventions are implemented and documented consistently. The guidelines specify the editorial practice and its encoding, while the schema defines the permitted XML structures. The final section, ‘Schema and elements used’, describes the schema.

Each section follows the pattern ‘Guideline’, ‘Technical implementation’ and ‘Example’. It sets out the editorial practice, followed by instructions for encoding it and selected examples from the project.

div.head: Editorial approach
div.p: The BEBB makes historical texts on the history of science accessible to researchers and a wider audience. Indexes of people, organisations, places and works help readers explore the material. The texts are searchable in full. Filters can narrow the results by criteria such as sender, recipient, date, place of sending or language.

Much of the descriptive metadata comes from the Basel Inventory of the Bernoulli Correspondence (BIBB). The editorial team supplies additional information. Digitised images of the letter manuscripts are being added on an ongoing basis.

div.head: Textual sources
div.p: The BEBB is a scholarly critical edition that usually takes a single textual witness as its basis. If several versions of a letter survive, the copy intended for the addressee is used as the principal witness. If that copy is lost, the closest surviving version is used, in order of preference: draft, manuscript copy, printed version and so on. In exceptional cases, such as loss of text, a further version is consulted.

All witnesses used to establish the text must be identified in the metadata. The principal manuscript is identified as the main version. The digitised images linked from the edition reproduce the witnesses actually used to establish the text.

div.head: Establishing the text
div.p: The edition aims to provide reliable scholarly texts that can be cited. Transcriptions are generally checked by a second person. Editorial interventions are documented in TEI XML or in footnotes.

Raw transcriptions also follow the editorial guidelines and are still undergoing review. The label describes an editorial stage. The notices for each text indicate which checks and indexing steps are complete. See ‘Revision history and editorial status’.

div.head: TEI XML as the basis of the edition
div.p: The edited texts, descriptive information and indexes are encoded in TEI XML, following the guidelines of the Text Encoding Initiative (TEI). The encoding records the wording, textual structure, editorial interventions and links to index entries.

Editorial decisions and encoding are closely connected. The encoding helps determine which features of the source can be recorded and analysed. The web application controls how they appear. When spelling is normalised, both forms are stored. The text-faithful version displays the historical spelling and the reading version displays the normalised spelling. See the description of the data model for further information.
Rules in the TEI Publisher ODD and the web application govern the display.
The root element TEI declares the TEI namespace as the default namespace (xmlns="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0").

The xml:id attribute holds the project-internal identifier for the file. For a letter file, it consists of the prefix B and the letter’s system number in the University Library Basel catalogue, for example B_991170515020505501. The date of the letter forms part of the filename, for example B_1714-05-15_991170515020505501.xml, and is omitted from the xml:id.

The TEI file identifier, filename and web address are distinct pieces of information. Links to the published text and the XML file are recorded in publicationStmt. See ‘Publication details and terms of use’.
The XML declaration specifies the XML version and character encoding, for example ?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?.
Letter files also reference the project’s entities.txt file through a DOCTYPE declaration. The entities defined in it help with data entry and are expanded into regular TEI XML before publication.

div.head: Line breaks
div.p: Line breaks in the source are recorded. Those that structure an address, a salutation or a signature remain visible in the reading version.
Line breaks are recorded with lb. The following cases are distinguished.

list.item: Ordinary line break. The line ends without a space and the next begins with lb. This break may be omitted in the reading version.

Within opener and closer, lineation is retained in the reading version. Elsewhere, lb type="forced"/ marks breaks to be retained in the reading version for reasons of layout, for example in inscriptions.
Word division. The division mark is recorded in pc type="hyphenation", and the following line break takes lb break="no"/.
Hyphen at the end of a line. The hyphen remains without additional markup and the next line begins with lb break="no"/.
Page break. lb follows pb directly.
Line break in a passage deleted in its entirety. lb type="deleted"/ suppresses it in the reading version. A division hyphen remains part of the deleted word.

div.head: Paragraphs
div.p: The paragraph structure of the source is recorded. This includes wider spaces within a manuscript line where these serve as paragraph breaks. Paragraphs introduced by the editors are explicitly marked.

Paragraphs are encoded in p. A space serving as a paragraph break within a manuscript line takes space type="paragraph"/, and an editorial paragraph takes p rend="editorial". Hanging indents are indicated by hanging or hanging-4em in rend.

div.head: Start of a page
div.p: Existing page or folio numbering is retained. If several numbering systems are present, the one used in the shelfmark reference governs. Blank manuscript pages and archival material digitised with the manuscript are marked separately.
For numbered letters without page numbers, the edition numbers the pages consecutively (1, 2, 3 …). Unpaginated enclosures take consecutive letters (a, b, c …) appended to the preceding page number.

The start of the page is marked before the first word with pb. n gives the page or folio number, with r or v for recto or verso in foliation. facs uses the image ID to point to the corresponding page in the IIIF manifest. The selected numbering is recorded once, so it is omitted from fw type="pageNum".
Blank manuscript pages take pb type="empty".
Archival material digitised with the manuscript, such as folders, bindings and covers, takes pb type="archival".

div.head: Catchwords
div.p: Catchwords are words or parts of words at the foot of a page that anticipate the beginning of the next page. They are recorded separately from the running text of the letter.
Catchwords are recorded with fw type="catch". place gives the position, for example bottom for the bottom margin.
When a paragraph spans two pages, the catchword may occur within p before the following pb. The paragraph remains a single unit.

div.head: Verse
div.p: Verse lines and their arrangement in line groups are reproduced.
A verse line is marked with l , and a line group with lg .

div.head: Annotations in the manuscript
div.p: Contemporary annotations and handwritten archival and postal markings are recorded. Their function, position on the page and scribal hand are described separately. The attribution of a hand is based on the evidence.

Contemporary annotations are recorded in note. hand gives the person’s xml:id from the index of persons. For an unidentified hand, use unknown. The following rules apply to archival and postal markings and to marginal notes.
Archival markings relating to custody and cataloguing take type="archival". Postal markings take type="postal" on note. An identified hand may also be recorded with hand.

Marginal notes take note place="margin". Use hand when the hand has been identified. To display the main text and marginal notes in separate columns, the enclosing div also takes rend="marginalia", for example div type="letter" rend="marginalia".

div.head: Figures and illustrations
div.p: Record figures where they appear or are first mentioned in the text. Distinguish original captions from editorial descriptions and explanations. For copied figures, document the person who drew the copy and the authorship of its source separately.

References to figures in external publications may include an image crop with a source credit. Where the reference is explicit, the crop appears at the point of reference. A footnote can explain an inferred reference that requires clarification.

Figures are recorded with figure. facs points to the part of the digitised image that shows the figure. hand identifies the person who drew it. Information about the authorship of a copied source can be given in a child note.

The figure element can contain the following child elements.
p for a caption in the source,
figDesc for an editorial description of the image,
note type="editorial" for an editorial footnote.
In the web view, a figure icon opens the image crop.

The filename for such an image follows the pattern ext_0001_01.png. The first four digits identify the external source, numbered consecutively across the project. The final two digits identify the figure within that source. The facs attribute on figure points to the locally stored PNG. Any original figure number or caption is reproduced in p. The bibliographic source, plate or figure number, and page or page ID in the external digital copy are documented in figDesc. Further editorial explanations may be given in note type="editorial".

div.head: Lists
div.p: Lists follow the wording and structure of the source as closely as possible. Filler and continuation marks are standardised.
A list is encoded in list and its entries in item.

div.head: Tables
div.p: Tables are reproduced as faithfully as possible, taking account of the original spatial arrangement and features that organise the information. The editors may give a clearer structure to uncertain, incomplete or nested arrangements where this is needed for a comprehensible representation that can be encoded. Content and discernible relationships are preserved. Uncertain editorial assignments are marked and explained. Empty areas are treated as text loss only where further evidence supports that reading.
Basic structure. Tables are encoded in table, rows in row and cells in cell. For rows and cells, role="label" indicates headings and role="data" indicates data.

Rules and alignment. table rend="boxed" indicates a border. Rules on rows or cells are encoded in rend with rule-above, rule-below, rule-left or rule-right, or their variants with double-rule-. Values for rules and alignment can be combined using spaces. Use table rend="astronomical" for astronomical tables set out in this way. Layout used solely for calculations within a formula is encoded in LaTeX.

div.head: Quotations
div.p: Quotations are recorded when they are marked as such in the source or identifiable from context. A quotation can be direct even if its wording differs from the source quoted. Significant changes in meaning and editorial source references are documented in an explanatory note at the relevant passage.
The quoted words are encoded in quote. Long quotations explicitly marked in the source take type="long". type="indirect" and type="paraphrase" are available for indirect quotations and paraphrases.
Source references supplied by the letter writer remain where they occur in the letter. Editorial source references are given in note type="comment". Identified sources are linked using rs.
An interjection by the letter writer within a quotation, such as «inquit» or «dit il», is encoded in said.

div.head: Quotations spanning paragraphs
div.p: A continuous quotation is recorded as a single unit, including when it spans several paragraphs or pages. Paragraph divisions and quotation boundaries follow the source.

Complete quoted paragraphs, including their p elements, are enclosed in a single quote type="long". Line and page breaks are recorded where they occur, using lb and pb. When a quotation spanning paragraphs starts or ends partway through a paragraph, the passage is reviewed individually. A common solution for encoding and web display is still pending for this kind of overlap.

div.head: Nested quotations and double underlining
div.p: A quotation within a quotation is recorded as a nested quotation. The wording and context determine whether double underlining marks a nested quotation or emphasis.

A nested quotation has its own quote within the enclosing quotation. Doubly underlined words take hi rend="uu". The text-faithful version retains the underlining. In the reading version, singly underlined passages are italicised, and doubly underlined passages are italicised with a single underline.

div.head: Quotation marks
div.p: The text-faithful version reproduces the form and position of the source’s quotation marks. In the reading version, direct quotations within running text use Swiss guillemets «…» and nested quotations within them use single guillemets ‹…›. Underlining throughout a quotation provides sufficient emphasis. Indirect quotations and paraphrases receive no added quotation marks.

Long quotations are indented and set in a slightly smaller type size in the reading version. Repeated quotation marks and marks enclosing the entire block are omitted. Direct quotations within the block may have their own guillemets.
For a direct quotation in running text that is unmarked in the source, rend="unmarked" triggers automatic guillemets in the reading version.
Montmort’s quotation has opening and closing quotation marks. The reading version replaces them with guillemets.

div.head: Mathematical formulae
div.p: Mathematical formulae are transcribed using the symbols, letters and mathematical operators in the source. Normalised notation may be added in a separate editorial step. Scribal corrections and mathematical errors in the source are documented separately from normalisation.

Mathematical formulae are marked with the formula element. Their content is encoded in LaTeX. Other TEI elements such as add, del, hi and abbr are omitted within a formula. Formulae may also occur in figure descriptions, notes and table cells.
‘Formula layout’ provides examples from letters and schematic encoding examples. ‘Normalising historical mathematical notation’ shows a source example in both historical and normalised notation.

div.head: Formula layout
div.p: When a mathematical expression continues onto the next manuscript line, the text-faithful version reproduces the break. Parts of a calculation deliberately set one below another or arranged in columns retain their spatial relationship. This applies, for example, to the two lines of a single numerator.

A formula set apart from the running text remains identifiable as a displayed formula. A calculation laid out over several lines is distinct from a table with independent columns of text or observational data.

Letters representing mathematical quantities or geometrical points should appear in the text as they do in formulae. Operator names and short pieces of text are set upright, and variables use mathematical italics. Commands used to control height or spacing must preserve the visible reading of the manuscript.
If a continuous expression can be split at a line break into two parts that can be rendered separately, encode them in two formula elements with lb break="no"/ between them.

A single arrangement of calculations is encoded in one formula element. LaTeX can align rows with aligned and columns with array. A LaTeX line break within a calculation is distinct from a line break in the letter text, which must be marked separately. rend="display" identifies formulae set apart from the running text.
Tables with independent columns of text, headings or observational data are encoded with table, row and cell. Their cells can contain formulae.
Letters representing mathematical quantities, such as variables or points, also use formula, so that they are displayed consistently in the text and in formulae.

Operator names and short pieces of text are set upright with \mathrm{…}, while variables remain in mathematical italics. A historical logarithm sign can be represented as \ell, depending on its written form and function. Continuation dots, proportion signs and differentials are recorded according to their mathematical meaning. The XML character & must also be escaped as & within LaTeX content.

Phantom commands such as \vphantom{…} control the height or spacing of visible characters. They introduce no additional reading of the manuscript. If a pair of delimiters is split across formulae, the LaTeX delimiters must be balanced within each formula, for example with an invisible counterpart \right. or \left..

div.head: Normalising historical mathematical notation
div.p: The text-faithful version preserves the mathematical notation of the source. A normalised form may be added for the reading version where modern notation makes the expression easier to read. The signs must be read with confidence and their mathematical function established from context. Normalisation changes only the notation. For mathematical errors, see ‘Mathematical errors in formulae’.

In choice, orig and reg each contain a complete formula element. The text-faithful version shows orig and the reading version shows reg. Repeated letters may be written as powers where they demonstrably indicate multiplication of the same variable.

Other cases include historical fraction notation, vincula and notation for proportions. A \times securely identified as a multiplication sign may be rendered as \cdot in the normalised reading. An abbreviated &c. is represented by \mathrm{etc.} where appropriate. Distinguish it from genuine continuation dots. Automatic substitution of \cdots or \ldots for every such abbreviation is inadmissible.

Distinguish the multiplication dot \cdot, the derivative dot \dot{…}, continuation dots and punctuation by function. A documented substitution for older LaTeX dot commands in a particular algebraic context does not establish a general rule. A superscript Latin ordinal o, a mathematical zero and a degree sign likewise have distinct functions.

Geometrical designations such as ABC, MJP or ed may denote points, angles, rays or segments. They should be interpreted as products of individual variables only where the evidence supports that reading. Identifying a letter such as I or J is a matter of reading the source. Normalising a sign securely identified as a mere separator is a separate decision. Angles and lengths can be recorded with measure. Mixed numbers such as 1545\frac{1}{2} retain their numerical value and are not reinterpreted as products.

Before approval, check that signs, numerical values, variables and groupings perform the same functions in both versions and that both render correctly. XML validity alone cannot establish correct LaTeX rendering or mathematical equivalence.
In the letter of 31 December 1718, Montmort quotes a passage by Brook Taylor. In the denominator, the squares are written as xx and aa. The reading version renders them as x^{2} and a^{2}.

div.head: Mathematical errors in formulae
div.p: A suspected or established mathematical error in the source is explained in an editorial footnote. If a correction can be justified, the corrected formula may be given there. The transcription retains the expression as transmitted. The normalised reading version also preserves its mathematical content.

A mathematically more plausible version still requires checking against the digitised image. Mark an uncertain reading. Individual signs or exponents borrowed from another version must be explicitly identified as such. The order of terms and table values follows the source. If an explanation presents them in a different order, make that clear.

Place the footnote at the relevant formula in note type="editorial". A mathematical expression in the footnote also goes in formula. A mathematical correction belongs in the footnote and is excluded from reg and from scribal correction markup with ana="corr".
Johann I Bernoulli gives \frac{1}{24} as the result of the fraction. The letter text retains this result. The footnote gives the mathematically correct value, \frac{1}{12}.
div.bibl: Johann I Bernoulli an Henri-Alexandre Barbaud (de Thiancourt), 3. Januar 1720, Bl. 122v (B_991170515371705501).

div.head: Scribal corrections in formulae
div.p: Record a correction made by the writer to a formula whenever it is discernible in the manuscript. Striking through a mathematical term, for example to show cancellation, counts as mathematical notation. Corrections important to understanding the passage may be explained in an editorial footnote.

For the time being, an identified scribal correction within a formula is marked only with formula ana="corr". When the formula is normalised, mark it on the formula in orig. The attribute identifies a correction in the manuscript. Normalisation and editorial mathematical corrections are recorded separately.
The extract from the historical reading shows how the scribal correction is marked.

div.head: Examples of common forms of historical mathematical notation and their encoding

item.p: A vinculum is a horizontal bar that groups terms. Establish its extent from the manuscript. An uncertain or mathematically questionable extent is only extended if the intervention is made explicit.
The vinculum is represented by \overline{…}. Modernised grouping notation can be given in the corresponding reg reading, where appropriate.

p.hi: Example of a formula with a vinculum
p.bibl: Nicolaus I Bernoulli an Pietro Antonio Michelotti. Basel, 24. Juli 1726, Bl. 174r (B_991170517024705501).

item.p: A radical sign without a bar is retained for a single number or variable. If the source separates the radical sign and the bar that follows it, the text-faithful version preserves that form. The two are joined in modern radical notation in the normalised version.

The radical sign without a bar, \sqrt{}, is retained for radicands consisting of a single number or variable. A separately written radical sign followed by a vinculum remains separate in the text-faithful reading, for example as \sqrt{\vphantom{0}}\,\overline{aa-yy}. Modern radical notation belongs in the normalised reading.

item.p: Historical notation for proportions is retained in the text-faithful version. Any modernised notation added must express the same ratio.
The two forms are presented in parallel with choice, orig and reg. The following example converts historical point notation into an equality of ratios.

Brackets often indicate the equality of terms, and the fourth proportional is calculated directly. For example, the formula a (AB) . b (BC) :: x (PQ) . y (PR) = bx/a brings together the proportion a : b = x : y, the premises a = AB, b = BC, x = PQ, y = PR and the result y = bx/a.

item.p: In historical polynomials, asterisks may mark the positions of terms with coefficient zero. The text-faithful version preserves them wherever they occur in the source.
Record the asterisk as * within formula.

Johann I Bernoulli uses four asterisks to mark terms with coefficient zero in a calculation of a sum of powers. \frac{1}{11}m^{11}+\frac{1}{2}m^{10}+\frac{5}{6}m^{9}\,*\,-m^{7}\,*\,+m^{5}\,*\,-\frac{1}{2}m^{3}\,*\,+\frac{5}{66}m Johann I Bernoulli an Abraham de Moivre, 9. April 1710, p. 7 (B_991170515105105501).
Historical symbols for geometrical objects are retained. Depending on the context, the same symbol can also denote the corresponding numerical measure.
The symbols \square (encoded as \square), \bigcirc (\bigcirc), \bigtriangleup (\bigtriangleup) and \angle (\angle) are retained. They can denote both geometrical objects and their numerical measures.

div.head: Authorial additions and deletions
div.p: Additions and deletions made by the author are recorded. When deleted text is replaced, the two actions are treated as a single correction. Illegible deleted text is marked as such.
Ordinary insertion marks that point directly to the position of an addition are omitted. Distinctive reference marks linking text written elsewhere to its insertion point are recorded.
Additions that the author made in the manuscript are marked with add.

Ordinary insertion marks such as small hooks, arrows or strokes that point directly to an insertion are omitted from the encoding. Use metamark for distinctive reference marks that link text written elsewhere to its insertion point.
Deletions by the author are marked with del.
If the deleted text is illegible, mark the illegible passage with gap.
When deleted text is replaced by an addition, encode the substitution with subst, enclosing del and add .

div.head: Authorial emphasis
div.p: Record the kind of emphasis used by the author. Alignment of lines and blocks is a separate feature, recorded on the element that represents the function of the passage.
Later marks of emphasis, for example by the recipient, are documented in an editorial note on the source.
Authorial emphasis is marked with hi . The rend attribute specifies the kind of emphasis. The available values are listed below.

list.item: Superscript sup
Underlining u
Double underlining uu
Mark in the margin mMM
Bold b
Overline overline

div.p: Alignment is specified on the element appropriate to the function of the line or block, p, dateline, salute or signed. center means centred, right means right-aligned, and right-block means a block positioned on the right with left-aligned text inside it. Apply alignment to the relevant component of opener or closer where appropriate. Indentation is encoded on the paragraph with the permitted values.

hi rend="c" is a deprecated transitional encoding. Existing occurrences are reviewed and migrated to appropriate block elements with rend="center". c will be removed from the schema and the presentation ODD once the data have been cleaned up.
Further instructions on hi appear on the guidelines for encoding typographical features page in the DTA documentation.

div.head: Reordering words in the manuscript
div.p: Record any reordering of words that the author indicates by numbering or other marks. The edited text follows the order indicated by those marks.
The affected text is marked with seg type="transposition".

div.head: Textual criticism
div.p: Editorial interventions are marked and explained in a textual note where needed.
Textual explanations are given in note type="editorial". Internal working notes are encoded with note type="internal".

div.head: Editorial corrections
div.p: Editorial corrections repair obvious errors, supply text or remove it. Normalisation of historical spelling is a separate operation.

div.head: Correction of scribal errors
div.p: Obvious scribal errors and incorrect punctuation are corrected, with the transmitted form documented. Historical spellings of proper names and titles are retained and identified through the indexes.

Within choice, sic contains the transmitted form and corr the corrected form. Corrections to words normally include the whole word even if only one letter is missing. The same structure is used for punctuation. Links to the indexes use rs.

div.head: Editorial deletion
div.p: Words written by mistake, for example accidental repetitions, may be deleted editorially. The transmitted text is documented.
Within choice, the word in question is placed in sic. An empty corr type="deleted"/ marks the deletion.

p.bibl: Pietro Antonio Michelotti an Nicolaus I Bernoulli. Venedig, 27. Juni 1718 (B_991170517053805501)

div.head: Editorial supplementation
div.p: The editors may supply omitted words and punctuation. These editorial additions are distinct from reconstructions of material once present but subsequently lost through damage. Supplied words appear in square brackets in the reading version.
Editorial additions are encoded with supplied. Whole words or longer additions also take rend="brackets". Reconstructed text lost through damage takes unclear. See ‘Uncertain readings’.

div.head: Illegible passages and text loss
div.p: Mark illegible or lost passages as gaps if the wording cannot be recovered. Explain the cause in a footnote if it matters for understanding the passage.
Use gap for gaps that cannot be reconstructed. Use unclear where a reading can be proposed or lost text reconstructed. Explain the gap in note type="editorial".
For portions deliberately left untranscribed, see ‘Omissions’.

div.head: Uncertain readings
div.p: Mark uncertain readings, including reconstructions of material once present but subsequently lost through damage. Mark a gap if no wording can be recovered.

Uncertain readings are encoded in unclear. Use reason="illegible" for writing that is difficult to read and reason="lost" for a reconstruction of lost text. Omit reason if the cause is unknown. Give any necessary explanation in an editorial footnote.

Readings encoded with unclear appear in grey with a dotted underline in both versions. On hover or keyboard focus, a tooltip explains the uncertainty or its cause. illegible displays ‘Difficult to read’, binding ‘Obscured by binding’ and lost ‘Text loss’. Without reason, the tooltip reads ‘Uncertain reading’.
Use gap for unreconstructable passages and supplied for editorial supplementation. See ‘Editorial supplementation’.

div.head: Omissions
div.p: Mark any portion deliberately left untranscribed for editorial reasons.
Editorial omissions are encoded with gap reason="editorial"/. The attribute distinguishes them in the encoding from illegible or lost passages. The same display rule applies as for other gaps.
The section ‘Enclosures’ gives an encoding example for an enclosure that has been transcribed only in part.

div.head: Abbreviations
div.p: Record abbreviations and expand those a general reader is unlikely to understand. Abbreviated proper names are retained in the text and identified through the indexes. When an abbreviation point coincides with a full stop, use a single point.

Historical abbreviation marks are preserved in the text-faithful version. A colon serving as an abbreviation point is represented by a full stop in the reading version. Abbreviation marks that stand for omitted letters are expanded according to their meaning.

Overlines are treated according to their function. In abbreviated words, the abbreviated form with the overline is retained and the expansion can be consulted as a reading aid. Overlines used as doubling marks over m and n are expanded to mm and nn respectively in the reading version.

Abbreviations are encoded in abbr. When an expansion is supplied, enclose abbr and expan in choice. In the web view, the abbreviation remains in the text and the expansion in expan appears in a tooltip.

When only the abbreviation mark is normalised, record its original and normalised forms with choice, orig and reg. Project entities are also available for specific abbreviation marks. A mark reproduced unchanged requires no choice.

An overline in an abbreviated word is recorded with hi rend="overline" inside abbr. Any expansion is given in expan and displayed in a tooltip. Use the corresponding project entities for doubling marks.
Supply missing abbreviation points with supplied. A point that also serves as a full stop is placed outside abbr.
Link abbreviated proper names with rs. Abbreviations within formulae do not take separate abbr markup.

div.head: Changes of language
div.p: Passages in another language are marked. Proper names, technical terms, currency names and individual loanwords are excluded from this rule. Titles of works in another language are marked if they consist of several words. In German texts, foreign-language expressions are considered in context.
For addresses, see ‘Address’.
Passages in another language are encoded in foreign with the xml:lang attribute. Language markup does not change the type style. Emphasis in the source is encoded separately.

div.head: Dates
div.p: Dates retain the wording of the source. Their chronological position is recorded as precisely as the source and context allow. This also applies to relative dates. Where only a date range can be established, record the bounds supported by the evidence.

Dates are encoded in date. when holds the standardised Gregorian date at the level of precision supported by the evidence, JJJJ, JJJJ-MM or JJJJ-MM-TT. For a date range, notBefore gives the earliest possible date and notAfter the latest. If only one bound can be established, use only the corresponding attribute. when is used separately.

div.head: Julian and Gregorian dates
div.p: Retain the date as written in the source. Standardise it to the Gregorian calendar for discovery. The calendar used in the source must be established from the evidence. Place or century alone is insufficient.
For a Julian date, when holds the standardised Gregorian date and when-custom the standardised Julian date. datingMethod="#julian" applies exclusively to when-custom.

calendar identifies the calendar of the visible date. Use #julian for a purely Julian date and #julian #gregorian for a double date. The values refer to the corresponding calendar entries in calendarDesc.

div.head: Transcription of special characters
div.p: Special characters are recorded according to their function. The relevant normalisation rules apply to abbreviation marks and diacritics.

div.head: Symbols
div.p: Symbols, for example for celestial bodies, units of measure and currencies, are retained. Establish their meaning from context and explain it where necessary.

Represent special characters with the appropriate Unicode character or a dedicated project entity. Enter Unicode characters directly or as numeric character references. Project entities contain the prescribed character encoding and, where applicable, its normalisation. choice is only needed when there is an alternative reading. Symbols used as abbreviations may be encoded with abbr.

div.head: Numbers
div.p: Arabic and Roman numerals are retained as transmitted. Points that simply separate a numeral or formula from the surrounding text remain in the text-faithful version and are omitted from the reading version. Sentence punctuation, abbreviation points and signs with a mathematical meaning are treated according to their function.

The numerical value requires no additional markup. Use &ndot; for a point to be omitted and &nddot; for a colon to be omitted. Both entities record the sign in orig and leave reg empty. For signs with a mathematical meaning, see the rules for mathematical notation.

div.head: Normalisation
div.p: The edition preserves the historical spelling and makes selective normalisations for the reading version while retaining the meaning of the text. The following sections specify these adjustments. For scribal errors, see editorial corrections. For formulae, see historical mathematical notation.

Within choice, orig contains the spelling in the source and reg the normalised spelling. If a punctuation mark is omitted, record it in orig and leave reg type="deleted" empty. For individual signs, see ‘Transcription of special characters’.
Schematic example of a comma in the source that is omitted from the reading version.

div.head: Diaeresis
div.p: A diaeresis present in the manuscript is retained in both versions. Missing diaereses are left as in the source. This rule applies regardless of the language of the text.

The dots over y customary in German Kurrent are preserved in the text-faithful version. The reading version uses y for this historical letterform. It is an exception to the general rule for diaereses.
Letters with a diaeresis reproduced unchanged are entered directly, without choice.
The historical y with two dots is recorded with &ydots;. The entity holds «ÿ» in orig and «y» in reg.
Schematic example. If the manuscript has «aër», both versions display «aër».

div.head: Capitalisation

list.item: Use a capital letter after a full stop that ends a sentence. After a semicolon, colon, exclamation mark or question mark, retain the capitalisation of the source.
Capitalise proper names and identifiable titles written in lower case, including abbreviated titles of works and journals, for example «actes» becomes «Actes».
In the reading version, capitals and small capitals are normalised to the usual capitalisation, for example «BERNOULLI» becomes «Bernoulli».
Internal capitals in proper names are generally retained, as in «NeufChâtel» or «ArchiLyceum». Other cases are decided in context.

div.p: If the case of a letter is ambiguous, follow the writer’s usage or modern usage. Such choices require no special markup. Deliberate normalisations of case are recorded in choice with orig and reg. The list of characters is under ‘Characters and XML entities’.

p.bibl: Jean Jacques de Mairan an Johann I Bernoulli. Paris, 9. Januar 1724, p. 1 (B_991170514804005501).

div.head: Latin texts
div.p: Diacritics are generally omitted in the reading version. The language-independent rule applies to diaereses. Abbreviation marks are expanded.
Normalisation of diacritics is recorded with choice, orig and reg. The characters and their normalised forms appear in the technical overview.

div.head: French texts
div.p: Clearly legible accents and the cedilla follow the source. Ambiguous accents are transcribed according to modern usage. Missing accents are supplied only when they distinguish forms, as in «à», «là» and «où». The oe ligature is represented as «œ».
Variable inflectional endings, such as a missing final s, may be normalised selectively if this clarifies the grammatical form and aids reading. Such cases are treated as normalisation.
Normalising additions of accents or endings are encoded with choice, orig and reg. Accents transcribed as written, the ligature and the cedilla remain part of the text.
In «je croi», the reading version supplies the final s. In «a l’epreuve», it supplies the accent on the preposition.
div.bibl: Johann I Bernoulli an Jean Jacques de Mairan. Basel, 5. Januar 1723, p. 1 (B_991170514804905501).

div.head: German texts
div.p: Diacritics are largely retained. The mark distinguishing u is treated as part of the letterform and is omitted from the separate markup. The letters i/j and u/v are rendered in upper or lower case according to their sound value. Intermediate forms are adjusted without separate marking.
When a clearly identifiable letter differs from the form indicated by its sound value, record the normalisation in choice with orig and reg. The character list is in the technical overview.
Schematic examples of normalisation according to sound value

div.head: Characters and XML entities
div.p: For abbreviation marks and other historical special characters, normalise only the relevant character or character sequence. Project-specific XML entities are available for this purpose. When the entity is expanded, the form in the source is represented in orig using g, and reg holds the normalised form. The definitions are maintained in entities.txt.

‘Special characters and abbreviation marks’ lists the characters in use, their normalised forms and their XML entities. Manuscript examples help identify them. Select an entity according to the written form and its meaning in the word concerned.

div.head: Opening of a letter
div.p: Record the salutation and dateline as components of the opening if they occur there in the source.
Encode the opening in opener outside a paragraph. Use salute for the salutation and dateline for the dateline. Specify alignment on the relevant component, for example on salute or dateline.

div.head: Closing of a letter
div.p: The closing may include a valediction, signature and dateline. Identify its boundaries from the function of these components, even when the manuscript does not set them apart visually. A signature written by another hand in a draft is also recorded as a signature.

The closing is encoded in closer. Its components are recorded with salute, signed and dateline. Link the personal name in the signature using rs. Indicate alignment on the relevant component, for example on signed.
In opener and closer, line breaks recorded with lb are retained in the reading version without requiring type="forced".

div.head: Notes of receipt and reply
div.p: Notes of receipt and reply are recorded as manuscript annotations. Identify the hand where it is known.
The annotation is encoded in note. The hand attribute points to the identified person in the index. See ‘Annotations in the manuscript’.

div.head: Postscripts
div.p: Postscripts are distinguished from the preceding body of the letter. Record each postscript as a separate unit.
Each postscript is encoded in its own postscript. The running text is divided into paragraphs with p.

postscript.p: P. S. Nondum accepi exemplaria Libri Dni De Monmort ex Gallia mihi apportanda, […]

div.head: Enclosures
div.p: Enclosures are documented as part of the surviving material. Editing them is optional. Editorial statements about authorship and source are kept separate from the text of the enclosure.

Printed enclosures are generally documented with a bibliographic reference and, where available, a digitised copy. Enclosures mentioned in the letter but no longer extant are documented in a footnote where possible.

If an edited manuscript enclosure has its own system number, record it as a separate document and link it to the letter. If a digital copy is inaccessible or cannot be published, give a bibliographic reference to the source.

Enclosures are described in accMat in the header. An enclosure encoded with its letter is placed in back, each in a separate div type="attachment". Within it, div type="editorialNote" contains editorial information and div type="attachment_text" the text of the enclosure.
Use gap reason="editorial" to indicate that a surviving enclosure has been left untranscribed. Give bibliographic references and links to separately edited enclosures in the editorial note.
Document a reference to a lost enclosure in a footnote, without creating a separate enclosure structure.

div.head: Address
div.p: Reproduce the lineation of addresses and link people and places to the indexes. Retain hyphens at line endings. Transcribe handwritten postal markings and document postal stamps and seals in the description of the source.

Record an address as a separate component of the letter regardless of its language. If the address is in a different language from the letter, its language does not require separate markup as a change of language.

Encode the address in address within opener or closer. Use a separate addrLine for each line of the source, without an additional foreign. Retain a hyphen at the end of its line without further markup.
Encode people and places with rs. For handwritten postal markings, see the rule for note type="postal" under ‘Annotations in the manuscript’.

div.head: Translations
div.p: Translations render the edited text in another language. Record their review status independently of the editorial status of the source text. A translation is considered reviewed once it has undergone a full scholarly check against the source text. Individual corrections alone are insufficient.
Under body, place translations in their own div type="translation" alongside the transcription. The required attribute xml:lang indicates the target language, de for German or en for English.

The required attribute status takes the value unreviewed until the scholarly review is complete and reviewed afterwards. An internal working translation also takes subtype="internal", independent of its review status.
The responsible person may be identified with resp. An optional xml:id ends in _trans_de or _trans_en, respectively. ana is omitted on the translation division.

div.head: Linking references to the indexes
div.p: Identify people, places, publications, manuscripts, letters and institutions mentioned anywhere in the letter. Personal and relative pronouns, and names and places within bibliographic titles, are excluded from separate indexing.

Link to an index entry or letter only when the identification is secure. Explain uncertain identifications in an explanatory note at the passage. Automatically suggested links are reviewed by an editor before they are accepted.
Mark references with rs. The type attribute identifies the category.

list.item: person for a person
place for a place
biblio for a publication or manuscript
letter for a letter
lostletter for a letter established as lost
organisation for an institution

div.p: If the identification is secure, key holds the xml:id of the index entry or letter document. For letters, use the identifier on TEI rather than the filename. Where a phrase refers to several identified entries, separate their identifiers with spaces.
If the identification is uncertain, omit key in the letter text. Possible identifications can be explained in a note at the passage, with links there to the relevant index entries.

div.head: Annotation
div.p: Summaries outline the contents of letters and form part of the basic annotation. Keywords may also be assigned. They identify the subjects discussed and provide the basis for developing a subject and thematic index.

Notes at individual passages explain their content or justify editorial interventions. Short editorial preliminaries describe the textual basis, provenance or editorial treatment. Substantial scholarly introductions are independent texts.
Summaries are recorded in the header under profileDesc/abstract. Under profileDesc/textClass/keywords, each keyword is recorded in its own term. Further rules and examples are under ‘Summary’.
Notes at individual passages are encoded with note.

list.item: type="comment" for explanations of the content
type="editorial" for notes on the establishment of the text

div.p: Mathematical errors in the source are also explained in an editorial footnote. See ‘Mathematical errors in formulae’. Use resp to identify the author of the note.
Internal working notes are recorded with note type="internal" and excluded from publication.
Short editorial preliminaries go under front in a div type="editorialNote".

Introductions to a correspondence are recorded in the corresponding companion file. When editing other texts without such a file, place the independent introduction in the edition file under text/front, within a div type="editorialIntroduction".
The preliminary note identifies the source used. This abridged extract from Daniel I Bernoulli to Tressan, 29 December 1750 omits additional markup to show the structure.
Der vorliegende Brief wurde nach der Fotografie von fo. 1r und fo. 2v der Handschrift in Aristophil, Vente inaugurale, Lot 122, transkribiert. […]

div.head: Links
div.p: Links point to further sources or information. The link text identifies the destination.
Link web addresses with ref and put the full destination address in target. Use rs, type and key for references to letters and index entries. See ‘Linking references to the indexes’.

div.head: Indexes
div.p: The indexes bring together information and references for people, institutions, places and works. Link authority records only when they clearly identify the same entity.
Internal working notes are kept in the editorial data and excluded from publication.

Entries for people, institutions and places are maintained as individual files under data/register. Their xml:id matches the filename without .xml. The combined index combined-indices.xml incorporates the individual files via XInclude.
Bibliographic data are maintained in the BEBB group library in Zotero and exported from it. Internal working notes are recorded in note type="internal".
Maintenance. XInclude references are generated with documentation/scripts/create-combined-index-list.py. Check changes in the individual files and their inclusion in the combined index.

div.head: Revision history
div.p: Substantive revisions are documented with a date and short description, newest first. The date records the documented editorial action in the index. Formatting and technical metadata maintenance are tracked separately.

The revision history is a list of dated entries in note type="revisionDesc", separate from revisionDesc in the TEI header. Documented editorial responsibility may be recorded on each item with resp. The Git history alone cannot establish that responsibility.

For entries in the index of persons, a person element contains at most one note type="revisionDesc" with exactly one direct list. Each item contains exactly one direct date with when="YYYY-MM-DD" and a non-empty description. The initials signing a short biography are recorded on note type="bio".

div.head: Index of persons
div.p: The index of persons records correspondents and people mentioned in the texts or annotations.
An entry is encoded in person. role distinguishes principal correspondents (main), other correspondents (correspondent) and mythological figures (mythological).
For documenting revisions, see ‘Revision history’.
The entry for Johann III Bernoulli carries role="main".

div.head: Identifiers and authority data
div.p: Every person is given a unique identifier. A GND number is used only if the authority record clearly identifies the same person. A similar name alone is insufficient.
If there is no matching authority record, a local entry may be created. An unidentified person can be described by a role attested in the sources.
For GND-based entries, the authority number appears in the identifier and in idno type="gnd". Local identifiers follow the pattern pers_resource_000001. Roles are recorded in roleName.

Replace an existing identifier only through a controlled update that also updates references to it. documentation/person-id-migrations.json documents completed changes. Redirects from old URLs require separate handling.
Samuel Werenfels has person xml:id="pers_DE-588-12209025X", and idno type="gnd" contains (DE-588)12209025X.
The entry ‘Tuteur’ records a tutor who has not been identified further and assigns a local identifier.

div.head: Names and name qualifiers
div.p: Each person has a preferred name. Record alternative names where relevant for identification or historical usage. Name qualifiers distinguish people with the same name. Distinct titles of nobility are recorded separately.

Given name and surname appear in forename and surname. persName type="reg" indicates the preferred name and type="alt" a variant name. Where applicable, subtype="birth" and subtype="married" distinguish birth and married names.
Generational qualifiers are recorded in genName and distinct titles of nobility in roleName. The Roman numerals in Bernoulli names belong in forename.
For names with nobiliary particles, the part used for sorting is recorded in surname and the rest in forename.
Preferred and married names in the entry for Dorothea Bernoulli, reduced to surnames and attributes.
For Niklaus Bernoulli the Elder, d.Ä. is recorded in genName. For Johann III Bernoulli, Johann III is recorded in forename.
For Pierre Rémond de Montmort, Montmort is recorded in surname and Pierre Rémond de in forename. Fenci has Conte in roleName.

div.head: Life dates and sex
div.p: Record life dates at the level of precision supported by the evidence. Preserve approximations and date bounds. Dates of activity are recorded separately from life dates.
Record sex where known.
For living people and people whose living status is uncertain, omit birth dates and birthplaces, including when these are available in authority records.

Record birth and death in birth and death, with date and, where applicable, placeName. when holds the date supported by the evidence, while notBefore and notAfter give date bounds. Approximate dates can be given as text in date. Dates of activity are encoded in floruit with date.
In gender, value="M" denotes male and value="F" female.
For Jean Formont de la Tour, um 1649 appears as text in date. For Roberto Poleni, the bounds are 1710 and 1716. For Fenci, 1719 is recorded in floruit.
Samuel Werenfels is recorded with M and Dorothea Bernoulli with F.

div.head: Short biography and sources
div.p: Short biographies cite their sources and retain existing author initials. Italicise titles of books and articles. Journal titles, reference works and edited collections follow ‘in:’ in roman type. Link the title of an online source.
The short biography is in note type="bio" and its source references in bibl. resp can identify the author of the biography. Encode titles of books and articles with hi rend="i".
Opening of the short biography and the HLS reference from the entry for Johann Ludwig Frey, abridged and with additional index markup omitted.

egXML.bibl:
Ulrich Gäbler,
Frey, Johann Ludwig, in: Historisches Lexikon der Schweiz, Version vom 3. März 2005; […]

div.head: Portraits
div.p: Verify the identity of the sitter and usage rights before including a portrait. Document the image credit, creator, licence and source page. Give priority to portraits selected by the editors over automatically suggested images.
Record the portrait in figure with graphic. figDesc contains the image credit, creator and licence information, and the link to the source page.
The entry for Johann Ludwig Frey includes a portrait with image credit, creator and licence information, and a link to the source page.

div.head: Index of institutions
div.p: The index of institutions covers universities, academies, libraries, authorities and publishers, among others. Distinguish institutions with the same name and take historical names into account when identifying them. Each institution receives a preferred name, and other attested names are recorded as needed. The description explains the institution’s nature, history and function, and cites its sources.

An entry is encoded in org. If a GND record identifies the institution as historically intended, give the entry an identifier such as org_DE-588-36146-X. Record the GND number in idno type="gnd", for example (DE-588)36146-X. If there is no suitable record, assign a local identifier following org_resource_000001. External references may be recorded in ptr.
In orgName, the preferred name is recorded with type="reg" and other names with type="alt".
The location goes in location with placeName and, where applicable, country.
The nature and historical function of an institution may be explained in note type="description". Cite sources with bibl. resp may identify editorial responsibility for the note.
The abridged name extract for the Gymnasium auf Burg shows «Gymnasium Marianum» as another name for the same institution. The dates are omitted here.

div.head: Index of places
div.p: The index of places records the geographical entities mentioned in the texts. Historical names and names in other languages are assigned to the same place where the identification is secure. Record the location where it can be established reliably.

A place entry is encoded in place. Entries may have GeoNames-based identifiers such as place_GEO-498817 or local identifiers such as place_WEI-gardenkip. Adding an authority record does not automatically replace an existing local identifier.
Names and name variants are recorded in placeName, with xml:lang identifying the language. The German name records the place category in type, for example Gemeinde, Verwaltungseinheit or Gewaesser.

In location, the country code is recorded in country. Where the location can be determined reliably, record WGS84 coordinates in decimal degrees in two geo elements, for longitude (decls="lon_wgs84_dd") and latitude (decls="lat_wgs84_dd").
External references, such as records in GeoNames, GND or Pleiades, must identify the same place. In ptr, record the URL in target and the source type in type.
Explanatory notes may appear in note type="description". resp may identify editorial responsibility for a note.
Two extracts from the entry for St Petersburg show the recorded names and geographical location.

div.head: Identification and linking
div.p: The bibliographic index records works mentioned in the texts and literature consulted in preparing the annotations. Links point to the edition, translation or version identified in each case. The wording of the reference in the letter is preserved.
Verify bibliographic details against the title page. Retain the historical spelling of titles. The bibliographic index and individual authors’ catalogues of works serve separate purposes.

The xml:id of the index entry consists of biblio_ and the Zotero key and matches the filename without .xml. corresp links to Zotero. In the edited text, record the identifier of an existing entry in key on rs type="biblio".
Michelotti mentions Checozzi’s article in the letter to Nicolaus I Bernoulli of 6 June 1716.

div.head: Structure of entries
div.p: For standalone works, record the bibliographic details of the edition concerned. For articles and chapters, also record the journal or collective volume and the location of the contribution within it.

Entries are encoded in biblStruct. analytic records the title and authorship of a contribution and monogr the details of the book or journal. author and editor distinguish authors and editors. Their names are recorded in forename and surname.

On title, level="a" indicates a contribution, level="m" a book and level="j" a journal. The entry type is recorded in type on biblStruct, for example book, bookSection, journalArticle or encyclopediaArticle.
Place of publication (pubPlace), publisher (publisher) and date (date) are recorded in imprint.
biblScope records the volume, issue or pages with unit="volume", unit="issue" or unit="page", respectively. series records the series with title level="s".
Links to sources may be recorded in note type="url". Exported working annotations are handled separately.

Maintenance. From the TEI export BEBB.xml, documentation/scripts/Zotero-Export_replaceIdsAndSplit.py generates the individual files and orders the child elements of monogr according to the schema. Corrections are made in Zotero. Zotero tags are exported as note type="tag" under note type="tags", including workflow annotations such as «Digitalisat nicht gesucht» (‘digitised copy not yet sought’). Access details may appear in note type="accessed".
The second part of the correspondence with Pierre Varignon illustrates an entry for a book. The article by Sebastiano Checozzi shows the details of the contribution, journal and page reference.
The following extract from the Varignon entry shows only the place, publisher and date.

div.head: References to letters mentioned in the text
div.p: Identify letters mentioned in the text wherever possible. Letters within the BEBB are linked directly. For the time being, letters outside the edition are cited bibliographically in a footnote, as are other manuscripts. Letters established as lost are explicitly marked as such.
References to BEBB letters are recorded in rs type="letter", with the xml:id of the letter document in key. A letter established as lost is marked with rs type="lostletter".
‘Links’ shows a link to a letter in the BEBB.

div.head: Subject index
div.p: Keywords in the header are the basis for developing a subject and thematic index. See ‘Annotation’.

div.head: Metadata
div.p: The metadata describe the edited texts, their sources and their editorial history. They combine information from the Basel Inventory of the Bernoulli Correspondence (BIBB) with information supplied by the editors.
The information is recorded in the teiHeader and organised into fileDesc, encodingDesc, profileDesc and revisionDesc.
The file description (fileDesc) contains the title, responsibilities, publication details and description of the sources.

div.head: Title (titleStmt)
div.p: The title identifies the edited letter or text. Former titles may be retained to document their history. The title of the edition as a whole is «Basler Edition der Bernoulli-Briefwechsel».

In titleStmt, title type="full" brings together the current title (type="main"), any former titles (type="alt") and the title of the edition (level="s"). For related texts outside the letter edition, author may identify the author.

Extract from the letter from Pietro Antonio Michelotti to Nicolaus I Bernoulli of 14 April 1714, abridged to show the main title and the edition title.
Pietro Antonio Michelotti an Nicolaus I Bernoulli. Venedig, 14. April 1714 Basler Edition der Bernoulli-Briefwechsel

div.head: Responsibilities and contributions
div.p: The edition names the editors responsible for each text, as well as other contributors and their roles. Contributions to individual letters are credited according to the work performed. The following roles are distinguished.

list.item: Establishing the text («Textkonstitution») means taking responsibility for the edited wording and the editorial readings.
Collation («Kollationierung») means checking the text against the source. Contributors may be named jointly for collation. Responsibility for establishing the text is assigned separately.
Basic annotation («Grundkommentierung») includes the summary and the essential research on people, works and subjects needed to understand the letter.
Scholarly annotation («Wissenschaftliche Kommentierung») provides more detailed explanations drawing on specialist research.

div.p: The optional role ‘Transcription’ («Transkription») may identify the person documented as having prepared the initial transcription if they differ from the person responsible for establishing the text.
Record the editorial work actually completed. Basic annotation requires more than partial research or links to the indexes alone.
Give the role as text directly in resp within editionStmt/respStmt and name the contributors in persName. Establishing the text and collation are separate roles, even when performed in the same step.

editionStmt also records the edition name in edition and funding in funder. editor identifies the people documented as having primary responsibility for editing the individual text. Project-wide responsibilities are given as respStmt in titleStmt.
Dated editorial steps in change within revisionDesc and the completed editorial stage in its status attribute are recorded separately. See ‘Revision history and editorial status’.

div.head: Publication details and terms of use
div.p: The editorial team of the Basel Edition of the Bernoulli Correspondence is responsible for publication. Record the place of publication, publication date, terms of use and links to the published version and its XML file.

A text included in a data release belongs to a larger publication. The version DOI identifies the complete data package. The individual text is identified by its own XML ID and its own web and XML URIs.

publicationStmt records the responsible body in authority, the place of publication in pubPlace, the publication date in date and the licence for the edited text in availability/licence. Links appear in idno with type="URLWeb" or type="URLXML", respectively. The publication date refers to the version published. The date of the letter is recorded separately.

Record membership in the data package in an additional seriesStmt under teiHeader/fileDesc. Its title identifies the data release. Place it after the existing seriesStmt elements for the correspondence and exchanges, and before notesStmt or, when there is no notesStmt, before sourceDesc. Use type="DOI" and subtype="data-package-version" on idno for the package’s version DOI. The subtype is a BEBB convention for the standard subtype attribute. For index fragments, record membership at package level or in the header of the published combined file.

Extract showing the body responsible for publication, the place of publication and the licence for the edited text.

(CC BY-SA 4.0)
Agreed header block for the planned BEBB beta data release.

Use only the version DOI to identify the beta data release. Omit the concept DOI and any placeholder for it. The published beta files are frozen, so the concept DOI will not be added to them retrospectively. The first regular release is planned for early February 2027 as a new version of the same Zenodo record. Its package is to include the concept DOI available at that point and a newly reserved version DOI. The concept DOI identifies the record across all versions. The version DOI identifies the specific package.

Under the planned release workflow, a separate step inserts the block into the approved beta snapshot only, before final checksums are calculated and the archive is built. Header updates preserve the release-managed block. Later changes to the working files belong to the ongoing edition and fall outside the archived beta snapshot.

div.head: Additional information about sources and other versions
div.p: Additional information may explain the dating, damage or later alterations to the source. Cite existing printed editions bibliographically. Identify other versions by their holding institution, shelfmark and a catalogue link.

In notesStmt, note type="generalRemark" provides general information about the source, while note type="print" identifies printed editions. Information about the extent of indexing and the provenance of the edition data is recorded in note type="erschliessbarkeit" and note type="dataGroup", respectively. Editorial status is recorded separately in revisionDesc.

Document another version in notesStmt/relatedItem/bibl. orgName names the institution, idno type="callNumber" gives the shelfmark and ref links to the catalogue record. For the source used in the edition, see ‘Description of the source’. For links to digitised copies, see ‘Facsimiles’.

General information about the source in the letter of 13 March 1706.

div.head: Description of the source
div.p: The source description identifies the witness used for the edition and documents its custody, physical characteristics and transmission. Describe the role of the manuscript in the composition or transmission of the text only where the evidence is secure.
The manuscript description is recorded in msDesc under sourceDesc. The type attribute may indicate the kind of version if it can be identified securely.

list.item: concept for a preliminary draft in outline or note form
draft for a fully worded draft
copy for a contemporary or later copy
excerpt for a deliberately made extract from a version
fragment for a version that survives only in part
fairCopy for a fair copy, whether or not it was sent
sentVersion for the version that was sent
otherForm for another version outside these categories

div.head: Holding institution, shelfmark and catalogue numbers
div.p: The holding institution and shelfmark identify the source. Additional catalogue numbers identify it in the catalogue systems used by the edition.

Within msIdentifier, record the holding institution in repository and the shelfmark in idno type="callNumber". Give each additional catalogue number in a separate altIdentifier containing idno. Its type attribute distinguishes ALMA_NZ (Alma Network Zone, BIBB field 001), ALMA_IZ (Alma Institution Zone, BIBB field 035) and ALEPH (former ALEPH system number).
Holding institution and shelfmark in the letter from Pietro Antonio Michelotti to Nicolaus I Bernoulli of 22 February 1715

div.head: Extent, dimensions and scribal hands
div.p: Record the extent and dimensions of the source, any surviving enclosures and any identifiable hands.

The information is recorded in physDesc. Under objectDesc and supportDesc, extent holds the extent and dimensions within it gives the dimensions. Enclosures are recorded in accMat. For editing enclosures, see ‘Enclosures’.
In handDesc, each handNote describes one hand. scribe identifies the role, for example author for the author’s hand. If the attribution is secure, persName can link to the person entry using key.
Extent and dimensions in the letter of 22 February 1715, in an extract from supportDesc

div.head: Place and date of the source
div.p: Record the place and date in the dateline as written in the source. Record the standardised date separately.

Under msDesc and history, origin contains the place in origPlace and the date in date. If the same date of sending also appears in correspAction type="sent", the standardised values must agree. The date of receipt is recorded separately. For historical calendars and year styles, see ‘Julian and Gregorian dates’.
Place and date in the source of the letter of 16 September 1758

div.head: Text genre
div.p: The genre indicates the kind of text being edited, for example a letter, speech or travel diary.
The genre is recorded in teiHeader/encodingDesc/classDecl/taxonomy/category/catDesc.
The letter of 14 April 1714 is classified as follows.

div.head: Correspondence (correspDesc)
div.p: Record who sent the letter, to whom, from where and when. If the date of sending is missing from the source, establish it where possible. Mark inferred data and date only as precisely as the evidence allows. Record the place of receipt if attested. Record a date of receipt only when it is given in a receipt annotation in the source.
Also record the letter’s membership in a correspondence and in the correspondence of an individual Bernoulli, along with its place in the sequence established by the editors.

In correspDesc under profileDesc, type on correspAction distinguishes sending (sent) from receipt (received). If the identification is secure, key on persName or placeName points to the xml:id of the index entry. Any supplied wording is encoded in supplied within placeName or date.

Record the standardised date on date. Use when for a specific date, from and to for an attested period, and notBefore and notAfter for inferred bounds. Justify inferred bounds from the source evidence. Standard attributes contain Gregorian dates standardised to the level of precision supported by the evidence (YYYY-MM-DD, YYYY-MM or YYYY). For historical calendars and year styles, see ‘Julian and Gregorian dates’.

In correspContext, the ptr types prev and next identify the preceding and following letters. Korrespondenz identifies exchanges between one Bernoulli and the other correspondent. Briefwechsel identifies all letters exchanged with that Bernoulli. target gives the stable xml:id of the target document, with the date component omitted for letters. The full names are given in seriesStmt as title with type="Korrespondenz" or type="Briefwechsel", respectively. See ‘Publication details and terms of use’ for the additional seriesStmt that records membership in a data release.
Sending details in the letter from Giovanni Poleni to Johann I Bernoulli of 25 November 1725, simplified extract.

div.head: Language of the letter
div.p: Record the language of the letter independently of the language of any summary or translation.
In profileDesc/langUsage/language, spell out the language name and give the language code in the ident attribute.
Language of the letter from Nicolaus I Bernoulli to Franz Christ of 5 April 1710. Lateinisch

div.head: Summary
div.p: The summary provides a brief, factual account of the main information conveyed and the subjects discussed in the letter. German summaries are written in Swiss Standard German. The language of the summary is independent of the language of the letter.

The summary is recorded in profileDesc/abstract/p. xml:lang on abstract identifies the language. The project currently uses deu and eng. If there is no summary, omit the paragraph. A list of people may appear on its own in abstract. If both are absent, omit the element.

Opening of the edited summary of the letter from Nicolaus I Bernoulli to Franz Christ of 5 April 1710.

div.head: People mentioned
div.p: The list imported from BIBB records people mentioned in the letter. It supplements the links to the index in the letter text and may be incomplete.
The list is encoded as listPerson within abstract. Each entry contains a person with persName, whose key attribute points to the index of persons.

Entry from the list of people for the letter from Nicolaus I Bernoulli to Franz Christ of 5 April 1710. Additional life dates are omitted.

div.head: Revision history and editorial status
div.p: The revision history records what was done, when and by whom. The editorial status identifies the last stage to have been completed in full: inventoried («inventarisiert»), transcribed («transkribiert»), collated («kollationiert»), basic annotation complete («grundkommentiert») or scholarly annotation complete («kommentiert»). In the regular workflow, a higher stage includes the preceding steps.

For editions taken over from earlier phases, the steps may have been performed in a different order. Their provenance is therefore documented separately. The review of a text-faithful version added later is recorded independently of the overall editorial status.
Inclusion in a data release is independent of the text’s editorial status. The release records the same editors and contributor credits, including collation, basic annotation and subject annotation.

Editorial steps are usually recorded as change in revisionDesc/listChange, most recent first. Dates are given at the level of precision supported by the evidence. when contains the date, while notAfter can, for example, indicate the latest date supported by the evidence. who identifies the person responsible where known. status on revisionDesc gives the editorial status.
There are also special values. gedruckt records an external printed edition. It does not indicate completion of a BEBB edition. generated is the technical status of generated companion documents.

For diplomatic encoding added later to letters that have at least been collated, ana="diplomatic-reviewed" on revisionDesc indicates that the encoding has been checked in full against the digitised image, and ana="diplomatic-unreviewed" indicates that the review is incomplete. A completed review must be explicitly documented.

div.head: Citing the edition and locating passages
div.p: When citing a letter, give the precise location whenever possible. Use the page or folio references adopted in the edition. Give page numbers with «p.» or «pp.», and folio numbers with «Bl.» and «r» or «v», for example «p. 24», «pp. 24–26» or «Bl. 12r».

To cite a specific archived text, give the version DOI of the data package together with the filename or XML ID of the text. For the distinction between package and text identifiers, see ‘Publication details and terms of use’.

The page or folio reference is given in n on pb. The image identifier in facs links the page to the digitised image. The suggested citation is based on the title, the people responsible for the edited text and its stable address.

div.head: Facsimiles
div.p: Digitised images of the edited sources are added on an ongoing basis and matched to the corresponding pages of text. Include image credits and terms of use where the supplying platform provides them. Where available, a direct link leads to the digitised image on the supplying platform.
In facsimile/graphic, the url attribute contains the address of the IIIF manifest. The manifest lists the images, their sequence and their associated metadata.
facs on pb links the start of a page to the corresponding image. n gives the page or folio reference. See ‘Start of a page’.
An additional direct link to the digitised copy is given in facs on msDesc and displayed in the metadata.
The project creates its own IIIF manifests for images supplied by the BEBB. The image assignments and page sequence are checked before publication.

div.p: The edition data are encoded according to these guidelines and checked against the BEBB schema. A successful schema check is one part of quality control, alongside editorial review and verification of the web display.

Validate against a verified version of the schema that corresponds to the data being edited. XML well-formedness, Relax NG validity and additional Schematron rules are checked separately.
